subject.title: [RFC] Context Provenance: Add source/volatility metadata to injected context segments

question: Should OpenClaw adopt model-visible inline provenance tags for injected context segments, or should source and freshness metadata stay in a runtime-owned context-engine contract?
rationale: The current behavior is missing, but the requested design changes core prompt shape and may affect cache stability, session-state semantics, memory output, and future config surface.

options.title: Review and narrow Phase 1
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/54830 as the candidate, but require maintainers to settle the inline tag format and proof expectations before merge.

options.title: Move provenance out of prompt text
options.body: Reject inline prompt tags for now and pursue structured runtime or context-engine metadata like the adjacent InputProvenance discussion.

options.title: Decline this direction
options.body: Close the RFC and linked PR if maintainers decide the token, cache, and model-compliance costs are not worth adding to core.

recommendation.title: Review and narrow Phase 1
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/54830 as the candidate, but require maintainers to settle the inline tag format and proof expectations before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has recent ownership signal in the prompt-cache and stable-context area most directly affected by inline provenance tags.
